q: Why was the worst day so bad?
answer:
Net profit was ₹-26,445 on 2026-10-09 — ₹9,734 worse than the weekday “usual” (≈ ₹-16,711) and ₹7,897 worse than the day before (₹-18,549 → ₹-26,445). The data shows the drop is mostly an accounting shift in ad spend versus contribution, not a single measurable upstream system failure.

What changed (numbers by order date)
- Ad spend rose vs its usual level and accounted for most of the swing: order‑P&L ad spend moved from a “usual” ₹52,139 to ₹60,102, an adverse effect of about ₹7,963 on net profit (≈82% of the net‑profit change vs usual).  
- Contribution fell modestly vs usual: product contribution margin went from ≈₹35,428 to ₹33,656 (≈₹1,772 negative effect on net profit).  
- Together these reconcile to the full drop — the accounting identity net profit = contribution margin − ad spend (P&L basis) matches the change.

Where it concentrated
- A small set of ads/campaigns carried the move. The campaign TH-383‑SUSPENDER‑29SEP and a few ads moved from zero to meaningful negative contribution (one ad contributed about ₹4,279 of the adverse change; another ≈₹2,876). Those few items together explain a large share of the swing versus the usual level.

Why (causal confidence)
- The diagnostic runs did not find a single supported external cause. We can say confidently what changed (higher P&L ad spend vs lower contribution) and where it sat (a few campaigns/ads), but the data did not surface a supported label such as a bid/budget edit, creative failure, pricing change or stock issue as “the cause.”

Worth checking
- Inspect TH-383‑SUSPENDER‑29SEP and the flagged ads for budget/bid/creative edits or unusually high delivery on low‑performing audiences on 2026‑10‑09.  
- Check order-level details for those ads’ credited SKUs to see if a small product mix or pricing/return event magnified the impact.
